First, we must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{-{x}^{2}+9x-16}{(x-6)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x-6}+\frac{B}{(x-6)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-6)^{3}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-6)^{3}$ and get

$$
-{x}^{2}+9x-16=A(x-6)^{2}+B(x-6)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=6,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-(6)^{2}+9(6)-16 & =A(6-6)^{2}+B(6-6)+C \\ 2 & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=5$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-(5)^{2}+9(5)-16 & =A(5-6)^{2}+B(5-6)+C \\ 4 & =A-B+2 \\ A-B & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=7$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-(7)^{2}+9(7)-16 & =A(7-6)^{2}+B(7-6)+C \\ -2 & =A+B+2 \\ A+B & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $A-B=2$ and $A+B=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2A & =2-4 \\ A & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

 
and substituting back into $A+B=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1+B & =-4 \\ B & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum:

$$
\frac{-{x}^{2}+9x-16}{(x-5)^{3}}=-\frac{1}{x-6}-\frac{3}{(x-6)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-6)^{3}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}+9x-16}{(x-6)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{1}{x-6}-\frac{3}{(x-6)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-6)^{3}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{1}{x-6}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{(x-6)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{(x-6)^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-6|+\frac{3}{x-6}-\frac{1}{(x-6)^{2}}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
